report_name: Ransomware Attacks Hit Record High, Disclosures Up 25% in 2026

threat_actors.name: Qilin
threat_actors.description: A prolific ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) group identified as the most active threat, responsible for 18% of all publicly disclosed attacks (1,358 victims) between April 2025 and March 2026. The group's activity surged by 443% year-over-year.
threat_actors.goals: Financial extortion through ransomware deployment and data exfiltration.

attack_patterns.name: Spearphishing Voice
attack_patterns.description: Attackers leverage AI to create deepfake audio for vishing campaigns, enabling highly convincing impersonations to manipulate human targets and bypass technical controls.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The core ransomware operation involves encrypting victim files to extort financial payments.

attack_patterns.name: Transfer Data to Cloud Account
attack_patterns.description: Data is exfiltrated from victim networks to cloud accounts as part of a double extortion strategy before encryption.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: Attackers frequently attempt to prevent system recovery by deleting volume shadow copies or destroying backups, hindering restoration efforts.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: Initial access is often gained by exploiting known, unpatched critical vulnerabilities in internet-facing systems, as evidenced by 43.5% of victims having such flaws post-incident.

attack_patterns.name: Windows Management Instrumentation
attack_patterns.description: WMI is noted as a common tool used by ransomware groups for lateral movement within a compromised network.

attack_patterns.name: Brute Force
attack_patterns.description: Indicated by hunting hints suggesting monitoring for a high volume of failed logon attempts (Windows Event ID 4625) as a precursor to ransomware attacks.

malware.name: Qilin
malware.description: A ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) payload deployed by the Qilin group. It is used to encrypt victim files and exfiltrate data for double extortion tactics.

tools.name: vssadmin
tools.description: Used by attackers to delete Volume Shadow Copies, a common tactic to inhibit system recovery from backups.

tools.name: wbadmin
tools.description: Used by attackers to delete backup catalogs to further hinder system recovery efforts.

tools.name: wmic
tools.description: The Windows Management Instrumentation command-line utility, likely used for lateral movement and execution within victim networks.

tools.name: PsExec
tools.description: Mentioned as a common administrative tool abused by ransomware actors for lateral movement.

identities.name: Manufacturing Sector
identities.description: The most victimized industry for the fourth consecutive year, accounting for 22% of all ransomware incidents (1,660 attacks).

identities.name: Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services
identities.description: The second most-targeted sector in the report, with 1,389 victims, making up 18.4% of the total.

identities.name: Construction Industry
identities.description: The third most-targeted sector, with 541 disclosed victims.

indicators.name: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
id: 2b8bde45-5b38-4208-93f6-2c6d48b2a40e
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common ransomware tactic to inhibit system recovery.
references:
  - https://blackkite.com/reports/2026-ransomware-report
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-26
tags:
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.impact
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'delete'
      - 'shadows'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects commands used to delete Volume Shadow Copies, a technique used by ransomware to prevent system restoration.

description: Detects the use of wbadmin.exe to delete backup catalogs, a common ransomware tactic to inhibit system recovery.
references:

  - attack.impact

indicators.description: Detects commands used to delete Windows backup catalogs, a technique used by ransomware to prevent system restoration.

indicators.name: Suspicious WMIC Execution for Lateral Movement
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious WMIC Execution for Lateral Movement
id: 8e1f2a3b-4c5d-4e6f-7a8b-9c0d1e2f3a4b
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of wmic.exe to execute processes on remote systems, a technique often used for lateral movement.
references:
  - https://blackkite.com/reports/2026-ransomware-report
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-26
tags:
  - attack.t1047
  - attack.execution
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\wmic.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/node:'
      - 'process'
      - 'call'
      - 'create'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of the Windows Management Instrumentation Command-line (WMIC) utility, which can be used for lateral movement.

indicators.name: Potential Brute-Force Logon Attempts
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential Brute-Force Logon Attempts
id: 5d6e7f8a-9b0c-4d2e-3f4a-5b6c7d8e9f0a
status: experimental
description: Detects a high volume of failed logon attempts (Event ID 4625), which may indicate a brute-force attack. This rule requires correlation over time to be effective.
references:
  - https://blackkite.com/reports/2026-ransomware-report
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-07-26
tags:
  - attack.t1110
  - attack.credential_access
level: medium
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 4625
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects failed logon attempts (Windows Event ID 4625), which, when occurring in high volume, can indicate a brute-force attack for initial access or privilege escalation.
